defects.scenario: process.on('unhandledRejection'/'uncaughtException', reportBootFailure) is installed once at module load and never disarmed, so it governs the ENTIRE process lifetime, not just the boot window the task scoped ('A boot that fails in this window can never again be silent'). It is registered before SentryService.initialize() runs (which happens later, inside bootstrapElectron); Sentry's OnUncaughtException integration defaults to exitEvenIfOtherHandlersAreRegistered:false (confirmed in node_modules/@sentry/node-core/build/cjs/integrations/onuncaughtexception.js) and counts our handler as a pre-existing 'other' listener, so it will NOT force-exit either. Concretely: a real uncaught exception hours into a normal session (e.g. an IPC handler throw unrelated to boot) previously terminated the process (Node/Electron default, or Sentry's own exit since it was the sole listener); after this change the process just logs one stderr line and keeps running in a possibly corrupted state, with the main window frozen or behaving unpredictably and no crash dialog, until the user force-kills it via Task Manager. In a packaged Windows GUI build launched without an attached console, fd 2 often has no valid handle, so boot-trace.ts's writeStderr (line 24-31) throws EBADF/EPIPE and is silently swallowed by its own try/catch -- meaning even the one diagnostic line is lost for the exact production audience this task cares about, while the crash-and-restart safety net that existed before is gone. This is disclosed as 'Open concern #3' in implementation-notes.md and mirrors apps/ptah-extension-vscode/src/main.ts's precedent, but that precedent governs one VS Code extension host (bounded blast radius, host process supervises restarts), not the whole Electron app process -- copying it verbatim is a scope mismatch against this task's own acceptance criterion, which named only 'this window'.
defects.note: Deliberate, disclosed trade-off, not a hidden bug -- but still an evidenced production-safety regression a robust implementation should have scoped (e.g. disarm/replace the handler once RENDERER_LOADED_STEP fires, or call app.exit(1) after logging for a genuine post-boot crash) rather than leaving the whole-process behavior change unaddressed.

defects.scenario: The regression pin for the core reordering claim is a source-text position check (readFileSync + string indexOf on wire-runtime.ts with comments stripped), not a behavioural test that exercises wireRuntimePreWindow/postWindow at runtime. It does fail against the pre-fix source (registerCodeExecutionMcpForSubagents( does not exist there, so at() throws), so it satisfies 'fails against old code', and this is an established, documented convention elsewhere in the same file (B1 ordering pins predate this task) -- but it cannot catch a future edit that preserves the matched substrings/order while changing what actually executes (e.g. moving the call into a dead branch, or into a .catch that never runs). The only genuinely behavioural coverage of the ordering-preserving guarantee (registration still completes before openWindowGate on the happy path) is the text pin at line 95-103, not an executed integration test.

mentorNote: Root cause is real and well-evidenced (measured timings, a deterministic slow-CLI repro that flips 0/3 to 3/3, electronApp.evaluate(() => 1) answering during every hang), and every ordering invariant I traced held up: startCodeExecutionMcp stays pre-window (B1's actual requirement -- live MCP port before the Thoth memory-scan LLM query -- needs only this half), the workspace-change-listener race guard is untouched and still synchronous with no await inserted, registerCodeExecutionMcpForSubagents in postWindow still runs before booter.openWindowGate() on every path (verified boot-heavy-services.ts: nothing runs until openWindowGate), settleOnAbort never rejects and never leaks an unhandled rejection (verified by its own 5 tests plus boot-coordinator.ts's startPostWindow wrapper), and session-starters (chat-session.service.ts, chat-ptah-cli.service.ts, gateway-chat-bridge.ts) all explicitly await their own ensureRegisteredForSubagents() through the same enqueueMcpOp queue before reporting mcpServerRunning, so no SDK query can run tool-less because of the reorder. bringUpSubsystems is preserved byte-for-byte in behavior for the VS Code host (post-init.ts unchanged caller) and is exported/tested directly. The only real, evidenced gap is D1: the never-silent instrumentation was applied as a permanent whole-process handler rather than scoped to the boot window the acceptance criteria named, with a concrete production failure mode (silent hang instead of clean crash, potentially with zero stderr output in a windowed build). It's disclosed, not hidden, and I would not block indefinitely on it, but round 1 should send it back for an explicit scoping decision rather than let a whole-app safety-net removal ride through unaddressed.
